narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 65% chance you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—meaning failure was judged more likely than passing. The strongest factor was your third-year class-rank decile: at 3, you were well below the average accepted student’s 5.79, and this lower standing pushed the prediction toward failure. The second strongest factor was your family-income bracket; being in the upper-middle group contributed toward the failure prediction in this applicant pool. The third strongest factor was your undergraduate GPA of 2.90, which is below the accepted-student average of 3.23 and also pushed toward failure. Your first-year decile and LSAT score were lower than accepted averages too, but they were not among the three features that most influenced this decision. Gender and race were not used in the prediction.

To improve a future application, focus on what you can change: strengthen your academic record, particularly advanced law coursework or a post-baccalaureate program, and seek admissions counseling on how to explain your third-year ranking. Consider retaking the LSAT if practice scores suggest meaningful improvement, and ask the admissions office for feedback. Reapply only after showing a clear upward academic trend and a stronger readiness profile.
